info.name: Phoenix Perpetuals API
info.description: The REST API, spec 1.0.0. Pick the live or sandbox environment and set apiKey in it.

exec: // one Idempotency-Key per send: a retry of the same request in the same run reuses it

request.description: The environment of the host you called, the version, the server time, and whether the trading engine is reachable. No key needed.
This API described as OpenAPI 3.1, the file the SDKs and these docs are built from.
Whether the environment takes requests, whether the trading engine is connected, and which features are on.
Every request budget and limit, as they stand now. Budgets are per minute; a request takes from each budget it belongs to, and the rate headers of each answer say what is left.
The key you called with: its access, the accounts it reaches, the limits you set on it and its budgets.
Every market you can trade, with its tick size, size step, leverage, fee and exposure cap. The list is complete: it never pages.

Every market's last price, its 24 h change, range and volume, and its open interest, in one call (the market data stream's stats channel sends the same every 5 s). The list is complete: it never pages. as_of: when these figures were read.
Get a market
The accounts your key reaches in this environment, newest first, with their rule. On the live host: your evaluation and funded accounts. On the sandbox host: your sandbox accounts.
Reserves a new sandbox account; it opens within moments (status pending, then active). Every account you open counts toward your sandbox accounts for life, see GET /v1/limits.
The account with its live risk (null while it is being opened).
Equity, open P&L, margin, exposure per market, the room to each loss limit, the profit target and the nearest liquidation: the figures of your dashboard, computed the same way.
Everything that decides whether an order goes through: the rule, the trading day, slippage bounds, margin, order limits, the limits you set on the key and its budgets.
Each objective (profit target, trading days) and each loss limit, with where it stands.

query.description: One point per closed trade, or per trading day.

request.description: Get the equity curve
One row per trading day with a trade or a payout (midnight to midnight New York), newest first.
The leverage and margin mode of each market on this account.
The leverage and margin mode new positions on the market use. Changing the leverage of an open position changes its margin.
Every open position, valued at the market price, with its liquidation and breach prices and the exits that protect it. The list is complete or the call fails: it is never partial.
Get an open position

query.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same filters.

request.description: Closed positions, newest first, each with the pieces it was closed in.
Closes the position, or part of it, at the market. No other order is touched.
Cancels every working order, then closes every position. A key limited to some markets does this on those only.

query.description: working: the complete set of working orders. history: past orders. all: both.
The order you placed through the API with this id.
next_cursor from the previous page, with the same filters.

request.description: Orders, newest first: working ones and past ones. Orders placed on a trading platform are listed too (source platform).

Places an order on the account. A market order waits a moment for its fill. When the engine's answer is lost on the way, the answer is 202 with status unconfirmed: read the order again (Location) rather than placing it again.
Get an order
Changes the size or price of a working order placed through the API, in place. Without an Idempotency-Key a change is sent once; with one, the same change sent again under it is done once.
Cancels a working order of the account, placed through the API or on a trading platform. When it filled first, the answer is 409 order_not_working.
What an order would do now, sent nowhere: whether it would fill, rest or be refused (and why), its price, fee, margin, the position after it and the room under the exposure cap. Any key may call it.
Cancels every working order of the account, from any platform, or only those of one market. A key limited to some markets cancels on those only.
Sets (or, with an empty object, removes) the exits a working order of the API places when it fills.

query.description: The id of the last event you have: the ones after it, oldest first. Absent: from the oldest kept.

request.description: What happened on your accounts, oldest first: the same events the account stream sends. Poll with after = the id of the last event you have (next_cursor of the previous page).
One event of the log, as the stream and the webhooks send it.

The take-profit and stop-loss legs this API keeps on the position: native orders on the engine, so they protect even when the API is away. Each group is at most the position: a take-profit fill trims the stop-losses by its size, the last fill cancels the rest.

Places, changes and cancels take-profit and stop-loss legs together, against the state you read: when the position or a leg changed since, nothing is done (409 exits_changed, with the state now). The legs are reduce-only and never larger than the position.

Starts a strategy on the account. trailing_stop and break_even change the position's exits (the answer is the exits strategy). The programs (oco, twap, vwap, scaled, chase) place orders for you: each one is checked as an order you place yourself, and listed under the strategy.

query.description: active: waiting or working. ended: completed, canceled or ended. all: both.
The strategy you created with this id.
next_cursor from the previous page, with the same filters.

request.description: The account's strategies, newest first, with every order each one placed.
Get a strategy
Stops the strategy and cancels its working orders (reason strategy). Orders that already filled stay filled.
Your endpoints in this environment. They are made, and their secrets rotated, in your dashboard only.
Get a webhook endpoint
Delete an endpoint
Queues a webhook.ping (test true) to the endpoint; read the delivery for the outcome. It calls your server: a trade key or app.

query.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same filters.

request.description: What was sent to the endpoint, newest first, with every try and what it answered.
Get a delivery
Queues the same event again, marked test (the same event id: your receiver can tell it already has it). It calls your server: a trade key or app.
Stops sending to it; its events wait (enable sends them).
Resume an endpoint
Every event an endpoint can receive, and the group that brings it.
Your TradingView alert links in this environment. Links are made, and their addresses rotated, in your dashboard only: the address is a credential.
Get a TradingView link
Revoke a TradingView link

query.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same filters.

request.description: Every alert the link received, newest first, refused ones included, with what each did and why.
Get an alert
Its alerts are refused (link_paused) until it is resumed.
Resume a TradingView link
How an alert message would be read, sent nowhere: the action, sizes, prices, exits and market, and with a link what it would do now.

query.description: next_cursor from the previous page, with the same filters.

request.description: Every execution with its price and fee, newest first.
